subject.title: Feature: Private Mode for demos and content creation

question: What hard privacy boundary should OpenClaw expose for private/ephemeral sessions, and which metadata or side effects, if any, may still persist?
rationale: The requested feature is a user-visible security promise that crosses protocol, persistence, memory, plugin, channel, and UI boundaries; automation cannot safely choose the threat model or compatibility semantics.

options.title: Design a hard private-session contract
options.body: Add an explicit session privacy flag and require every persistence and plugin boundary to prove no private content is read from or written to durable stores before exposing the UI toggle.

options.title: Ship only a narrow no-history mode
options.body: Limit the first implementation to transcript/history suppression and clearly document that memory, tools, artifacts, and plugins are not yet covered.

options.title: Defer until broader privacy architecture
options.body: Leave the issue open but avoid adding config or UI until maintainers finish a broader privacy/security design for session state and plugin persistence.

recommendation.title: Design a hard private-session contract
recommendation.body: Add an explicit session privacy flag and require every persistence and plugin boundary to prove no private content is read from or written to durable stores before exposing the UI toggle.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this issue as the canonical private-mode tracker and is the strongest recent routing signal for the session/security boundary.
